actions.description: Close the Nicole Washington pilot — this tick, binary. Rachel has already sent the closing ask: 'I want to know whether the $800 pilot makes sense for you right now.' She reads the word-of-mouth: Nicole Washington is actively verifying her employment status, maintaining savings deposits, and has been flagged in the inbox as responding to Rachel's $800 pilot proposal directly. That means a response is likely this tick. If Nicole says yes, Rachel delivers the scope document within 48 hours — it is already drafted — and considers the pilot open. If Nicole says no or has not responded, Rachel sends one final message: 'Following up from last week. Yes means I send the scope document today. No means I check back in 60 days. Either is fine.' Then she stops. No third follow-up. She has been building to this close for three ticks. It resolves here.
actions.expected_outcome: Rachel receives a definitive answer from Nicole Washington. If yes, the $800 pilot opens — Rachel's first paying freelance client after eleven ticks of preparation. If no, Rachel immediately identifies one new potential first client this week from her existing network or from the auto-row business environment. Either outcome closes the uncertainty and redirects her energy to the next concrete step.

actions.description: Have the 20-minute referral call with Angela Wright — the one Rachel proposed and followed up on last tick. If Angela has agreed to the call, Rachel goes in with a specific two-way proposal: Angela refers clients who need marketing communications support — displaced workers who need to present themselves professionally as they transition, small businesses emerging from the auto-row contraction that need visibility — and Rachel refers clients who need workforce transition consulting. Rachel brings one concrete example to the call: a small business owner who just reduced staff and needs to communicate that change to customers without losing them. She positions herself as the person who knows how to do that for businesses operating in economic disruption. If Angela has not responded to the call proposal, Rachel sends one brief, final scheduling message: 'I have 20 minutes blocked Tuesday or Wednesday at 10am or 2pm. Either day works for me — which would work for you?' She does not send a third outreach if this one is also ignored.
actions.expected_outcome: The referral call with Angela Wright happens or Rachel gets a definitive non-response. If the call happens, a mutual referral arrangement is established — Angela routes displaced workers who need communications support to Rachel, Rachel routes clients who need workforce transition support to Angela. This is the highest-upside relationship in Rachel's current network: Angela is routing a growing population of displaced workers who need exactly what Rachel offers.

actions.description: Write and publish a second LinkedIn piece this tick — specifically about marketing through economic contraction. The angle: when local employment drops to 50% and the spending index hits 26, the businesses that stay visible and human on social media are building relationship capital that converts to sales when spending recovers. The piece includes one specific, actionable recommendation that a small business owner could implement this week without hiring anyone. It is not a pitch. It is a demonstration of Rachel's ability to translate macro economic conditions into practical communications guidance. The piece is also a signal to potential clients who are watching the same data and looking for someone who can help them respond to it. It is visible to potential employers, potential freelance clients, and the network of displaced professionals who may need marketing support in their own transitions.
actions.expected_outcome: Second LinkedIn post published, establishing Rachel as a consistent voice on marketing through disruption — not a one-time poster but someone who shows up when the data demands it. Visibility to potential clients in the auto-row business environment and the displaced worker community. This costs two hours and circulates indefinitely.

actions.description: Begin active job search in parallel with the freelance pipeline — not as the primary strategy but as a concurrent income safety net. Rachel's savings runway is 5 months with zero income. She cannot afford to run the freelance pipeline as the sole track and wait 3-4 months for it to produce revenue. She updates her resume this week to reflect her most recent marketing campaign outcomes, adds a section on digital content strategy and disruption communications, and identifies 3 specific marketing manager or director roles at healthcare organizations or financial services companies — sectors with stable employment through economic downturns. She is not broadcasting job-seeking. She applies to the 3 roles quietly. A salary offer does not replace the freelance practice — it extends the runway while the practice builds to financial viability.
actions.expected_outcome: Three targeted job applications submitted to stable-sector marketing roles. Rachel has both a freelance pipeline and a salaried employment track running simultaneously. The job search does not compromise the freelance positioning — she frames herself as a marketing professional with a specialist practice in disruption communications, which is true and is exactly the credential that stable-sector employers value during an economic contraction.
